title: Zero-shot generative models design HER2 antibodies, with 71 low-nanomolar binders among 421 characterised
summary: Shanehsazzadeh et al. (Absci) described generative models for de novo antibody design against HER2 without further optimisation, combined with high-throughput screening of about 10^6 HCDR variants; binding rates were 10.6 percent (HCDR3) and 1.8 percent (HCDR123), 71 of 421 characterised binders had low-nanomolar affinity by SPR, 11 were functionally equivalent or better than trastuzumab, and one showed about 3x higher cell-based potency. Preprint, not peer-reviewed at this version; a later journal version should be checked. Abstract-level review.
ai_technology: Generative deep learning models for antibody design

evidence.tested: Designed antibodies were expressed and measured by high-throughput screening and SPR, with comparison to trastuzumab (per abstract).
evidence.unknown: Peer review, in vivo activity, the reach beyond one target and the model details were not assessed; one organisation authored and tested the designs.
evidence.ai_role: Generative models proposed HCDR variants that were then screened for binding.

source_review.scope: abstract and bibliographic metadata (Europe PMC); full text not assessed
